thread:
Maya (Sec): ALERT: our org-wide GCP workload identity pools have a handful of service accounts with overly broad principal bindings discovered during a config audit. This enables actAs for non-service identities. Immediate remediation required.

infra-bot: Scan 2026-03-21T09:12Z -> 12 service accounts with wildcard or group bindings allowing broad impersonation. Report: https://go/internal/gcp-wif-audit

Helen (CloudInfra): Can you list the affected projects?

Maya (Sec): Affected projects: redwood-core, redwood-ci, model-serving-prod. Full list in the report. Action plan: 1) remove wildcard bindings, 2) enforce least-privilege principals, 3) enable IAM deny rule for future wildcards, 4) rotate any keys/tokens for affected identities.

Liam (SRE): Is there an enforcement window?

Maya (Sec): Enforcement steps: 2026-03-23 00:00 UTC - automatic policy will block new wildcard bindings; 2026-03-28 00:00 UTC - we will remove existing wildcard bindings and notify owners. If removal breaks a pipeline, open an exception (see below).

Zoe (Platform): We should publish a migration snippet for Workload Identity Federation (WIF) best practices. I can PR a template to infra/docs.

Maya (Sec): Good. Quick CLI to find suspect bindings:

```
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=PROJECT | grep -A2 "members:" | grep "principalSet://"
```

Helen (CloudInfra): For automation, use `tools/gcp_wif_prune.py --org redwood` which will generate a remediation plan and open tickets for owners. Use dry-run first.

Liam (SRE): If we remove a binding and a job fails, how do teams recover?

Maya (Sec): Failures will show as "permission denied: iam.serviceAccounts.actAs" in logs. Recovery: submit an infra-support ticket with justification and migration ETA; we can temporarily re-grant a scoped principal for up to 24h while you migrate to a narrowly-scoped service account or workload identity pool membership. Exceptions require infra-oncall + sec approval.

Zoe (Platform): Also enabling audit-level logging for iam.serviceAccounts.actAs across affected projects. That will help triage after removals.

infra-bot: Reminder: run `scripts/list_wif_bindings.sh > wif-report.txt` and attach it to your exception requests.

Maya (Sec): Please prioritize production-facing services and CI runners. We'll publish a status snapshot 2026-03-24 18:00 UTC. If you need help, DM me or tag @infra-oncall.

Liam (SRE): Acknowledged; running the tool now in dry-run.

Helen (CloudInfra): I'll schedule a migration window and post the project-level PRs
